attributes.probed_form: FIVE probes, all reverted; the tree is byte-identical to HEAD. (1) SECOND-KERNEL CONSTANTS AS LITERALS: `if (distance > sItemZero) { ... sArrowFloorYOffset * estimate * (sNewtonThree - estimate*estimate*distance) ... }` -> `if (distance > 0.0f) { ... 0.5 * estimate * (3.0 - estimate*estimate*distance) ... }`, four refinement steps. 42 -> 23 words at 122/122. The whole kernel proper, +0x160 to +0x1cc, went BYTE-IDENTICAL to retail, including all four fnmsub operand triples. (2) THE SAME LEVER ON THE FIRST (flyby) KERNEL: count-asymmetric, 123 vs 122. Cause read from the aligned view and named: the flyby block already reads sItemZero for `sphere[3] = sItemZero;`, so that load is shared with the guard; spelling the guard `0.0f` creates a SECOND constant and a second load. Re-run with the guard left as `sItemZero` and only the refinements literal: back to 122/122 and 23 words, and the first kernel's own registers were unchanged either way - so the first kernel's refinement spelling is inert and only the second kernel's pays. (3) GUARD-ONLY DECOMPOSITION: second kernel's guard as `0.0f`, refinements left extern. 42 words AND the +0x10c relocation moved from @sItemZero to an anonymous entry - strictly worse on both axes, which is what isolates the refinement constants as the whole lever. (4) REFINEMENTS-ONLY DECOMPOSITION: second kernel's guard left as `sItemZero`, refinements as `0.5`/`3.0`. 23 words with +0x10c still naming @sItemZero and its register now matching retail's f4 exactly; only +0x114 and +0x11c move to anonymous entries. This is the minimal-damage form and the one banked in `hypothesis`. (5) THE v1 RECORD'S MANDATED FORM, REFUTED: `f32 zero = sItemZero; f64 half = sArrowFloorYOffset; f64 three = sNewtonThree;` declared in the else-branch before the for-loop, kernel rewritten to use `zero`/`half`/`three`. 42 words - identical to HEAD. Reading the extern into an f64 local before the loop does NOT reproduce the literal form's allocation, so v1's 'spell the two refinement constants as f64 locals initialised before the loop' is measured dead. (6, on top of form 4) SEPARATE PARTIAL TEMP: `distance = dx*dx + dy*dy; distance = dz*dz + distance;` -> `f32 partial; partial = dx*dx + dy*dy; distance = dz*dz + partial;`. Count-asymmetric, 123 vs 122 - but informative rather than merely negative: it moved +0x158 to retail's exact `fmadds f0,f6,f6,f0` for the first time, and then overshot at +0x15c by putting `distance` in f0 as well, where retail uses f5.
attributes.residual: CAPPED ON A TRADE, and the trade is the deliverable. The rule stays and still closes 42 words. THE MECHANISM, from the aligned raw view: both kernels hoist four values into volatile FPRs before their loop or branch - the squared distance, the 0.0f guard constant, and the two f64 refinement constants 0.5 and 3.0 - and retail's descending assignment is {distance, guard, half, three} in BOTH kernels. Ours, with the constants spelled as extern reads, is {half, three, distance, guard}: not a shift, a scramble. Spelling the two REFINEMENT constants as literals restores retail's relative order exactly and takes the function from 42 to 23 words, which is the largest single movement any lane has recorded on this function. WHY IT WAS NOT KEPT: the literal spelling makes MWCC emit its own anonymous .sdata2 entries, so two relocations that previously named the target's own pool objects (@sArrowFloorYOffset at 0x80346FB0, @sNewtonThree at 0x80346FC8) now name @@432/@@433. The two project arbiters DISAGREE about whether that is a regression - `fndiff --relocs` resolves addresses and reports `relocation sets IDENTICAL (16 reloc(s), addresses resolved)`, exit 0, while `defake_gate check` compares symbol NAMES and reports `MOVED-AWAY-FROM-TARGET ... our OLD symbol matched it, the new one does not`, exit 1 - and AGENTS.md makes the gate's exit 1 a revert instruction. There is a further reason not to decide this unilaterally: the extern spelling is not incidental, it was deliberately introduced by attempt.items-extern-literal-sweep.20260831.v1 as a matching lever, so overturning it in this TU reverses an accepted decision. Note for whoever decides: the names sArrowFloorYOffset and sNewtonThree are the splitter's inventions for what are almost certainly MWCC's own anonymous pool entries for the literals 0.5 and 3.0 in retail's source (`sArrowFloorYOffset` names a 0.5 double, which is evidence of exactly that mis-naming), so the literal form is very likely the more faithful reconstruction and the gate's name comparison is the coarse arbiter here - but that is an argument, not a measurement, and it belongs to the integrator.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Run `python tools/gdl/fndiff.py game/world/items DistanceToClosestPlayer --relocs` on the 23-word body. If it reports the relocation sets DIFFERENT, the trade is not a conflict at all - the literal form is simply wrong and the cap is ordinary. Measured 2026-09-03 on exactly that body: it reports `relocation sets IDENTICAL (16 reloc(s), addresses resolved)` and exits 0, while `defake_gate.py check game/world/items` on the same body exits 1 with `MOVED-AWAY-FROM-TARGET: 'sArrowFloorYOffset' -> '@433'`. So the conflict is real and the two arbiters answer different questions - names versus resolved data.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the four hoisted-constant registers in each kernel, the f31 accumulator agreement at +0x1bc/+0x1c4, the fmadds destinations at +0x74/+0x78 and +0x158/+0x15c, and every relocation symbol at +0x88, +0x8c, +0x10c, +0x114 and +0x11c were read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 122-instruction body, in HEAD and in each probe.
hypothesis.statement: The 19 words the storage-class lever closes are BANKED AND REPRODUCIBLE IN ONE EDIT (spell the second kernel's two refinement constants as the literals 0.5 and 3.0 instead of sArrowFloorYOffset and sNewtonThree, leaving the guard as sItemZero); what blocks the keep is a two-arbiter conflict, not a missing idea, and resolving that conflict is the next lane's step 1 - it is a decision, not a probe. The surviving 23 words then decompose into exactly two clusters, both of the same shape: at +0x74/+0x78 in the flyby kernel and +0x158/+0x15c in the loop kernel, retail accumulates the first two squared terms into the SCRATCH register f0 and materialises `distance` only at the final fmadds, while we materialise `distance` at the first fmadds and update it in place; and at +0x130/+0x138/+0x148 retail reuses the register that held pos[0] for the dx subtraction (`fsubs f6,f6,f0`, in place) while we write to a fresh register. Both are the same 'fresh versus in-place' asymmetry PointLineDist2D's record named, now measured on a second member.
